newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BTP posts record profits, sees growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BTP posts record profits, sees growth.

text.p: LONDON - British speciality chemicals firm BTP Plc, posting its 16th consecutive year of record profits, on Tuesday predicted further earnings growth despite sterling's strength.
BTP's pretax profits rose 8.0 percent to 48.2 million pounds ($78.8 million) for the year ended on March 31, excluding exceptional charges in the previous year.
BTP raised its full-year dividend by 5.0 percent to 11.75 pence per share and said it would maintain a progressive dividend policy.
The profit growth came in spite of the pound's rise, which weighed down earnings by about 2.6 million pounds.
"It shows that the BTP group is very resilient to all that the world throws at us," chief executive Steve Hannam told Reuters in an interview.
"The effect (of sterling) we've seen in the second half will continue through to the next year, assuming there's no change. But in terms of impact on business, I think the worst is over," he added.
BTP's shares surged seven percent, rising 19.5 pence to 287.5 by 1015 GMT to rank among the top percentage gainers on the London Stock Exchange.
Along with record profits, BTP named a new finance director, appointing Ken Greatbatch to the post after Rob Martin resigned to pursue other interests.
Greatbatch was previously chief executive of Laporte Australia Ltd, part of speciality chemicals firm Laporte Plc.
Hannam said the pound's strength could hurt earnings this year by more than 5.0 million pounds, but BTP's profit growth should more than offset the impact.
The recent acquisition of fine chemicals maker PCR Inc should help boost earnings, adding 2.5-3.0 million pounds to pretax profits in the first year of ownership.
BTP expected to maintain the 12 percent compound annual growth rate in earnings it had chalked up over the past 12 years, Hannam said.
"We see sustained growth. The underlying growth of the divisions will provide the opportunities to continue to grow at the rate we have done," he said.

BTP's Biocides and Fine Chemicals division posted the strongest performance among its units, reporting an 8.5 percent rise in operating profits to 28.6 million pounds on a 13 percent increase in sales to 151 million.
The fine chemicals unit accounted for two-thirds of last year's 19.1 million stg capital spending budget.
BTP planned to spend just over 20 million pounds on capital investment projects this year.
Hannam said the company was looking for further acquisitions to boost its offerings for the pharmaceutical and agrochemicals industries.
"We will be looking for further bolt-on acquisitions in that area to increase our chemistry set," Hannam said.
BTP bought PCR from Harris Speciality Chemicals in April 1 for about $72.2 million. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
